Sound Familiar?

Problems I help businesses fix

If customers can’t find you, they find your competitor. These are the most common visibility problems I work on — and how I approach each one.

01 — LOCAL SEARCH

Not showing up when customers search nearby?

Your Google Business Profile, categories, services, photos and reviews decide whether you appear in Maps and “near me” results. My approach: audit your profile, fix categories and business details, build a local landing-page and citation plan, and set up a simple review workflow.

02 — ORGANIC VISIBILITY

Website gets visits, but few inquiries?

Traffic without action usually means weak service pages, unclear calls-to-action, or pages that don’t match what people actually search for. My approach: keyword and intent research, stronger service pages, internal linking, and clear next steps on every page.

03 — COMPETITORS

Competitors dominate local results?

Competitors ranking above you are doing specific things — better content, stronger profiles, more relevant links. My approach: competitor analysis to find the gaps, then a prioritized plan to close them step by step, honestly and sustainably.

04 — ADS & WEBSITE

Paying for ads or a website that doesn’t convert?

Ad spend and a slow, confusing website waste budget fast. My approach: tighten campaign structure and landing-page alignment, improve site speed and mobile experience, and track what actually leads to an inquiry.

How I Work

A clear process — no guesswork

You always know what’s happening, what it costs, and what comes next. Here’s how every project runs.

1

Discover

We talk about your business, customers, competitors and goals. I listen first, recommend second.

2

Audit

I review your website, Google profile, content and visibility to find what’s holding you back.

3

Plan

You get a prioritized plan with deliverables, timeline and a clear quote — before any work starts.

4

Execute

I do the work: optimization, content, website changes or campaigns — with updates as I go.

5

Measure & Improve

Simple reporting on visibility and inquiries, plus honest next steps to keep improving.

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Straight answers, before you spend anything.

SEO usually takes a few months of consistent work to show meaningful ranking and traffic improvements. Small fixes — like a corrected Google Business Profile — can help quickly, and I’ll show you progress monthly so you can see movement, not just promises.
No — no honest SEO can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google. Rankings depend on Google, your market and your competitors. What I guarantee is proper, white-hat work, clear priorities, and honest reporting on what improves.
Yes — local and Maps visibility is my specialty. I optimize your Google Business Profile, categories, services, photos, citations and local pages so nearby customers are more likely to find and choose you when they search.
Yes — I build and redesign WordPress websites. They are fast, mobile-friendly and SEO-ready, and I can help with ongoing updates and optimization if you need it.
You get a simple, plain-language report covering what was done and what comes next. It includes work completed, visibility and inquiry changes where measurable, and the next steps planned — no padded reports or vanity numbers.
Yes — most projects start with an audit. Send me your website and Google profile link through the contact form and I’ll review where you stand and what I’d fix first.
To start, I only need your business details, your website if you have one, and any access you’re comfortable sharing. We agree the scope and quote first — nothing starts without your approval.
Both — one-off projects and monthly work are available. Audits, profile setup and website builds work well as one-off projects, while ongoing SEO, content and ads are usually monthly. We’ll pick whichever fits your goal and budget.
The best SEO service for a small business is one that focuses on local customers, clear reporting and work matched to your budget. That means Google Business Profile optimisation, local keyword targeting, quality link building and helpful content — combined with honest timelines and no guaranteed-ranking promises.
Yes — I offer Pinterest marketing and Pinterest SEO. That includes keyword-rich boards and pin titles, scroll-stopping pin designs, Idea Pins, and traffic strategies that send Pinterest visitors to blogs, Etsy shops and affiliate sites. Beauty, home, food and lifestyle niches perform especially well — see my haircut guide in the writing samples.
Yes — I write Amazon affiliate review articles and buying guides. I research buyer-intent keywords and write honest pros and cons readers trust, so the content sells without hype. You can read my KetoSana review in the writing samples to see the style.
